lines: How does sunscreen actually stop a sunburn?
Sunlight carries invisible rays called UV, and they're what burn your skin.
Most sunscreens soak up those rays and turn them into a tiny bit of heat.
Mineral ones use tiny white particles that sit on your skin and block them.
But it wears off with sweat, water and towels!
So put more on about every two hours, and right after swimming.
